label: Well-Adjusted Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They demonstrate strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions, with anxiety scores near floor level and depression and loneliness scores well below typical thresholds of concern.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.79), suggesting robust social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.28), well below clinical concern thresholds
Near-zero anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.04), indicating very low generalized anxiety
Moderate and controlled screen/internet use (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment, which may serve as a protective factor for mental health

label: High-Distress Digitally Immersed Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores (mean 1.72), PHQ-9 depression scores (mean 1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety scores (mean 2.14) are all in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress across all three dimensions. With 181 respondents in this cluster, the profile represents a substantial subgroup characterized by compounded mental health burden despite advanced educational attainment.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores indicating persistent feelings of social disconnection
Higher depressive symptom severity suggesting frequent low mood, fatigue, or loss of interest
Notably high anxiety symptoms — the highest among the measured distress indicators
Extended daily screen time exceeding 5 hours, potentially reflecting both occupational demands and coping or avoidance behaviors
Co-occurrence of all three distress dimensions, indicating a compounded psychological burden rather than isolated symptoms
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the significant and overlapping mental health challenges faced by this group
